title: Germination — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define a repeatable germination workflow that preserves seed-lot identity, moisture/oxygen/temperature context, sanitation, radicle handling and failure evidence without presenting one method as universally best.

excludedUntilValidated: fixed germination time for every genotype/lot
overwatering as a default response to delayed emergence
discarding failed seeds without recording lot/method context

claims.statement: Cannabis seed germination depends on viable seed and suitable water, temperature and oxygen conditions, so method records should preserve the environment in which each lot was tested.
claims.boundary: The evidence does not support one universally superior germination container or technique.

claims.statement: Germination performance should be calculated from a defined lot/sample and observation window rather than generalized from a few successful seeds.
claims.boundary: Observed sample performance should not be converted into a guaranteed whole-lot rate without an appropriate sampling design.

claims.statement: Excess moisture and poor sanitation can complicate germination and early establishment, supporting controlled moisture and clean handling rather than keeping seeds continuously saturated.
claims.boundary: Exact moisture targets should be validated for the chosen method and substrate rather than copied as a universal number.

claims.statement: Emerging radicles and young seedlings are mechanically vulnerable, so transfer methods should minimize avoidable handling damage and preserve lot/plant identity.
claims.boundary: The SOP should define handling principles, not claim that one transfer timing fits every method and genotype.

claims.statement: Failed, delayed or contaminated germination batches should retain method, lot, environmental and sanitation evidence so cause can be investigated before repeating or changing the process.
claims.boundary: A failed batch should not automatically be attributed to genetics when method or storage conditions are unresolved.
